ROSE Lab.title: When and How Much to Imagine: Adaptive Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Visual Spatial Reasoning
ROSE Lab.authors_text: Shoubin Yu, Yue Zhang, Zun Wang, Jaehong Yoon, Huaxiu Yao
ROSE Lab.summary: This paper introduces AVIC, an adaptive framework that optimizes visual imagination in spatial reasoning by selectively invoking it based on evidence sufficiency, enhancing efficiency and accuracy.
ROSE Lab.debug_abstract: Despite rapid progress in MLLMs, visual spatial reasoning remains unreliable when correct answers depend on how a scene would appear under unseen or alternative viewpoints. Recent work addresses this by augmenting reasoning with world models for visual imagination, but questions such as when imagination is actually necessary, how much of it is beneficial, and when it becomes harmful, remain poorly understood. In practice, indiscriminate imagination can increase computation and even degrade performance by introducing misleading evidence. In this work, we present an in-depth analysis of test-time visual imagination as a controllable resource for spatial reasoning. We first study when static visual evidence is sufficient, when imagination improves reasoning, and how excessive or unnecessary imagination affects accuracy and efficiency. To support this analysis, we then introduce AVIC, an adaptive test-time framework with world models that explicitly reasons about the sufficiency of current visual evidence before selectively invoking and scaling visual imagination. Finally, to further learn this gating and planning behavior without any annotation of when and how much to imagine, we introduce AVIC-R, which trains the policy via GRPO from QA-correctness rewards and penalties by imagination cost. Across spatial reasoning benchmarks (SAT, MMSI) and an embodied navigation benchmark (R2R), our results reveal clear scenarios where imagination is critical, marginal, or detrimental, and show that selective control can match or outperform fixed imagination strategies with substantially fewer world-model calls and language tokens. Our AVIC-R surpasses strong proprietary baselines including GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 while invoking the world model less often. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of analyzing and controlling test-time imagination for efficient and reliable spatial reasoning.

ROSE Lab.title: Breaking the Discretization Barrier of Continuous Physics Simulation Learning
ROSE Lab.authors_text: Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Nan Wang, Lilan Peng, Kun Wang
ROSE Lab.summary: The paper introduces CoPS, a data-driven approach that overcomes discretization limitations in continuous physics simulation learning by utilizing multiplicative filter networks and multi-scale graph ODEs.
ROSE Lab.debug_abstract: The modeling of complicated time-evolving physical dynamics from partial observations is a long-standing challenge. Particularly, observations can be sparsely distributed in a seemingly random or unstructured manner, making it difficult to capture highly nonlinear features in a variety of scientific and engineering problems. However, existing data-driven approaches are often constrained by fixed spatial and temporal discretization. While some researchers attempt to achieve spatio-temporal continuity by designing novel strategies, they either overly rely on traditional numerical methods or fail to truly overcome the limitations imposed by discretization. To address these, we propose CoPS, a purely data-driven methods, to effectively model continuous physics simulation from partial observations. Specifically, we employ multiplicative filter network to fuse and encode spatial information with the corresponding observations. Then we customize geometric grids and use message-passing mechanism to map features from original spatial domain to the customized grids. Subsequently, CoPS models continuous-time dynamics by designing multi-scale graph ODEs, while introducing a Markov-based neural auto-correction module to assist and constrain the continuous extrapolations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CoPS advances the state-of-the-art methods in space-time continuous modeling across various scenarios.

中国科学技术大学.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
中国科学技术大学.summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

中国科学技术大学.title: MorphTwin: Enriching Deformable Material Responses from Videos for Morphable and Interactive Physical Twins
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Haoqin Hong, Ding Fan, Fubin Dou, Tianyu Huang, Yuzhuo Chen
中国科学技术大学.summary: MorphTwin enhances deformable material simulations from videos by independently controlling deformation responses, achieving significant accuracy improvements over existing methods in real-time applications.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: Reconstructing interactive physical twins from video requires accurately capturing how objects deform while maintaining efficient simulation. We observe that reproducing motion in a video does not guarantee correct responses to new forces when the physical representation restricts how an object can deform. In spring-based twins, coupling between volume and shape responses creates such a limitation. We present MorphTwin, which enriches local deformation modes to capture and independently control these responses while retaining standard spring forces and explicit simulation. To support interpretable material editing and transfer, we use offline calibration to map shared relative response changes to stiffness updates on each reconstructed graph. Under identical inverse settings on synthetic scenes, MorphTwin reduces the mean absolute error of Poisson's ratio by 75.8% and the mean relative error of Young's modulus by 22.1% compared to PhysTwin. We introduce an egocentric stereo and RGB-D benchmark covering interactions with objects of varying stiffness. Real-world experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and up to 14.4% lower future tracking error than PhysTwin at interactive speeds.

中国科学技术大学.title: Minimal Memory for Correctable Visual Continuation
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Xiyang Zhang, Yuanhe Tian, Hongzhi Wang, Yan Song
中国科学技术大学.summary: The paper presents a method for efficient visual continuation using Coherent Archive Memory (CAM) to store and update geometric summaries for accurate future frame generation and correction.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: Given past images and known actions, visual continuation generates future frames from one evolving scene state. Keeping this state revisable matters when an object reappears or a later view changes an earlier interpretation. Once past images cannot be replayed, a summary sufficient for current rendering can lose candidates needed after correction. We establish matching sparse and dense bounds on the bits needed for later correction under stable observations and bounded disagreement. For static streams at the stated smoothness and margin scales, correction incurs at least logarithmic overhead in one dimension and polynomial overhead in higher dimensions. Coherent Archive Memory (CAM) stores geometric summaries with exact updates under clipped expansion and coordinate assignments, then uses historical existence constraints to select one state for all requested frames. Exhaustive photographic tests show strict worst-truth image-risk gains from joint witnesses, while controlled neural continuations recover positions hidden in the current view.

中国科学技术大学.title: VisualTalk-Bench: Evaluating Question-Driven Avatar-Led Video Explanations
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Xin Zhang, Tujie Xu, Zhiyi Chen, Xiaodong Zhang, Sicheng Yang
中国科学技术大学.summary: VisualTalk-Bench evaluates avatar-led video explanations for user questions, highlighting challenges in gesture alignment and establishing benchmarks for content accuracy and visual consistency.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: Advances in video generation and avatar synthesis enable new ways to answer user questions through visual explanations. This task requires a system to formulate a correct answer, translate relevant information into visual material, and deliver the explanation through an avatar's speech and actions. Existing benchmarks rarely assess whether avatars point to the visual content being discussed. We introduce VisualTalk-Bench for question-driven avatar-led video explanations in finance and Chinese and English education. It includes 800 curated reference videos and 100 independent evaluation requests, assessing Content Factuality, Speech-Visual Consistency, Visual Quality, Motion Smoothness, and Avatar-Content Pointing. Yet end-to-end video generators often struggle to align gestures with specific visual targets. To explore this challenge, we develop Avatar-O Agent, a modular reference implementation with explicit interaction planning. Experiments across six agents show that factual precision and visual quality do not guarantee accurate pointing. A 26-participant study comparing four agents finds that Avatar-O Agent receives the highest average ratings for visual guidance, perceived pointing accuracy, and explanation effectiveness. We will release the data and code.

中国科学技术大学.title: WAMotor: Accelerating World Action Models via Speculative Inference under Dual Nonuniform Denoising Dynamics
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Zexun Lin, Yuan Feng, Xike Xie
中国科学技术大学.summary: WAMotor enhances World Action Models by addressing dual nonuniform denoising dynamics, achieving significant speedups while preserving task success rates through innovative speculative inference techniques.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) unify world modeling and action generation for robotic control by integrating flow-matching velocities, yet suffer from high multi-step denoising latency. Recent studies have explored speculative inference to accelerate WAMs by drafting and verifying denoising steps in parallel. However, existing methods either require training task-specific draft models or overlook critical WAM denoising dynamics when reusing past velocities as drafts. We revisit the denoising dynamics of WAMs and identify a dual nonuniformity that breaks standard velocity-reuse assumptions: velocity smoothness is nonuniform as adjacent velocity residuals differ sharply at early and final steps, so reuse there yields large residuals, which nonuniform integration time steps further translate into local state errors that accumulate into the final action distribution. Accordingly, we formalize this by theoretically deriving a trajectory error tolerance bound that characterizes how velocity residuals and integration time steps affect the final action distribution. Based on this, we propose WAMotor, the first speculative inference method tailored to the dual nonuniformity in WAMs. It selects reliable anchor velocities by deferring speculation and employs time-step-aware verification that scales acceptance thresholds by integration time step size. WAMotor offers plug-and-play benefits, enabling seamless integration with prior WAMs. Extensive evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and LIBERO-Plus show that WAMotor achieves 2.86$\times$--4.28$\times$ end-to-end speedups while maintaining task success rates. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Overdue-Lin/WAMotor

中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Nan Wang, Lilan Peng, Kun Wang

机器人控制实验室.title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Linjia Kang, Binhan Jiang, Juan Yang, Zhiqin Song, Xiangsen Wu
机器人控制实验室.summary: StarTV-Agent enhances traffic scenario understanding by integrating policy learning and experience evolution, achieving improved performance and efficiency through adaptive reasoning and workflow reuse.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible. During training, Role-Sensitive Process Optimization (RSPO) combines process advantages with terminal advantages, while Weakness-Driven Demonstration Learning (WDL) provides validated teacher demonstrations targeting the student's weak questions. During inference, Lightweight Adaptive Workflow Reuse (LAWR) enables a fast path by selecting suitable workflows and binding task-specific arguments and resource references, while a slow ReAct-based path handles tasks without suitable workflows. We further design label-free feedback based on execution completion, workflow adoption, and cost savings to guide workflow reuse and memory updates. Across three challenging benchmarks, StarTV-Agent achieves up to 8.0% relative performance improvement, while reducing token consumption by up to 52.1%.

机器人控制实验室.title: Homeward: No Place Like the Training View
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Mingyang Lyu, Yinqian Sun, Gongce Cao, Guobin Shen, Yuhao Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: Homeward is a training-free adapter that transforms uncalibrated camera observations into training views, significantly improving vision-language-action policy performance across varied camera setups.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies implicitly assume that third-person cameras remain fixed at their data-collection poses; once a camera is bumped, remounted, or swapped at deployment, task success degrades precipitously even though the underlying task and robot remain unchanged. We present Homeward, a training-free, plug-and-play observation adapter that canonicalizes observations from an uncalibrated deployment camera back into the training view for frozen VLA policies. Our design stems from a closed-loop diagnostic paradox in simulation: while re-rendering perturbed views into the training camera with oracle geometry recovers much of the lost performance, substituting an off-the-shelf feed-forward 3D foundation model can leave the policy worse off than applying no correction at all. This degradation concentrates on the thin, articulated robot arm, which feed-forward depth prediction tears and scatters - yet the arm's exact 3D state is already known from robot kinematics. Homeward exploits this asymmetry: it estimates what is unknown - camera parameters and static scene depth - from the live RGB frame and a single training-view reference, and renders what is known - the moving robot links - directly from the kinematic model. Evaluated across $\sim$300,000 closed-loop episodes spanning four frozen VLAs, Homeward boosts success across all 1,599 camera variants of LIBERO-Plus from 62.5%, 76.5%, 68.0%, and 3.6% to 77.6%, 95.1%, 91.2%, and 26.4% for OpenVLA-OFT, $π_{0.5}$, $π_0$, and OpenVLA, respectively. Without any scene fine-tuning or deployment camera calibration, Homeward extends to 6-DoF random placements, focal-length changes, and, with per-step pose estimation, continuous intra-episode camera drift, while matching or surpassing a calibrated, scene-trained view-synthesis baseline on three of four policies on LIBERO-Plus.

机器人控制实验室.title: Hyper-RED: Scalable Event Pre-training via Semantic Hypergraph Distillation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Meisen Wang, Zhiqiang Tian, Wei Bao, Chengjie Wang, Shaoyi Du
机器人控制实验室.summary: Hyper-RED introduces a scalable image-to-event pretraining framework using hypergraphs to enhance semantic alignment and transferability between images and event data, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Event cameras have shown great potential for robust visual perception, yet scaling event representation learning remains challenging due to the scarcity of large-scale annotated event data. Pretrained image models provide scalable semantic supervision, but existing image-to-event methods rely on rigid pixel-wise or token-wise alignment that overlooks modality discrepancies in texture, density, and appearance, potentially causing semantic collapse and limiting transferability. To address this issue, we propose Hyper-RED, a simple, painless, and scalable image-to-event pretraining framework that transfers high-order semantic structures from images to events. Hyper-RED uses hypergraphs to model and align high-order semantic associations among multiple image and event tokens, enabling cross-modal knowledge transfer while accommodating modality-specific differences rather than enforcing rigid one-to-one correspondence. Specifically, given a paired event--image sample, Hyper-RED leverages DINOv3 to extract spatial token representations and constructs image, event, and cross-modal semantic hypergraphs, where each hyperedge connects multiple semantically correlated tokens. We further introduce a hypergraph relational distillation loss that imposes complementary intra- and cross-modal constraints, enabling the event encoder to inherit image-derived semantic organization while preserving local relational consistency and event-specific characteristics. Experiments on three tasks across five event datasets demonstrate consistent scaling from ViT-S to ViT-L and state-of-the-art performance (Fig.1). The code is available at: https://github.com/meisenwang/Hyper--RED.

机器人控制实验室.title: MyoChallenge 2025: A New Benchmark for Human Athletic Intelligence
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Cheryl Wang, Chun Kwang Tan, Balint K. Hodossy, Eric Lyu, Jun Guo
机器人控制实验室.summary: MyoChallenge 2025 establishes a benchmark for athletic motor intelligence, combining musculoskeletal models and machine learning to enhance robotic performance in sports tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Athletic performance represents the pinnacle of human motor intelligence, demanding rapid choices, precise control, agility, and coordinated physical execution. Replicating this seamless combination of capabilities remains elusive in current artificial intelligence and robotic systems. Concurrently, understanding the biological mastery of these movements is hindered because complex muscle coordination is rarely measured in vivo due to the limitations of physical equipment. To bridge this fundamental gap in understanding, MyoChallenge at NeurIPS 2025 established a pioneering benchmark for motor control intelligence in sports, leveraging high-fidelity musculoskeletal models within physics simulation combined with machine learning-driven algorithms. The competition introduces two distinct tracks emphasizing either upper or lower limbs control: a table tennis rally task utilizing a biomechanic upper limb composed of an arm with a hand and a trunk; and a soccer penalty kick using a biomechanic model of legs and a trunk. Marking the fourth iteration of the MyoChallenge series, this event attracted almost 70 teams and over 560 submissions globally, uniting a diverse community ranging from physicians and neuroscientists to machine learning experts. The competition facilitated the development of several state-of-the-art control algorithms for a musculoskeletal system capable of sports agility, leveraging techniques such as physics-based motion planners, on-policy behaviour cloning, hierarchical planning, and muscle synergies. By integrating standardized tasks and physiologically realistic models into the open-source framework of MyoSuite, MyoChallenge'25 serves as a reproducible and reusable testbed to accelerate interdisciplinary research across machine learning, biomechanics, sports science, and neuroscience. Project page: https://www.myosuite.org//myochallenge/myochallenge-2025.

机器人控制实验室.title: Composable Driving Style for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiashu Li, Jiaxing Chen
机器人控制实验室.summary: YOUDrive enables composable control of driving styles in end-to-end autonomous driving through a vision-language-action planner that adjusts behavior via learned task vectors.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. We propose YOUDrive, a vision--language--action planner for continuous and composable driving-style control. Each teacher's behavior is distilled into a task vector, a learned parameter update that induces a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining the backbone. Conditioned on these directions, a flow-matching decoder models a multimodal trajectory distribution and generates kinematically feasible motion alternatives. We introduce the Style Alignment Score (SAS) to describe human-referenced kinematic behavior after safety and task gating. On NAVSIM navtest, a single coefficient monotonically controls assertiveness across six teacher-derived personas, while PDMS remains above 0.90 across the tested individual and blended configurations, reaching 0.954. Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.

机器人控制实验室.title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Boyu Chen, Jiaqi Liang, Xini Ding
机器人控制实验室.summary: GroundingPI is a state-of-the-art grounding foundation model that enhances physical intelligence in robotics by improving object localization and manipulation through advanced multimodal training techniques.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

机器人控制实验室.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Changli Tang, Jie Yang, Tianyi Wang, Lei Li, Daoze Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: WeMM-Video introduces advanced bilingual omni-modal foundation models for superior video understanding and reasoning, outperforming proprietary counterparts and promoting open-source research.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

机器人控制实验室.title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Wei Dai, Jinkun Liu, Jiayi Chen, Han Liu, Wenbo Ding
机器人控制实验室.summary: EmbodyAgent enhances vision-language models into effective embodied agents through a novel post-training framework combining data synthesis, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, achieving significant performance improvements.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

机器人控制实验室.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Wai Ka Sun, Waiyiu Pong, Bowen Wang
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents passage-conditioned navigation, enhancing wheeled-legged robots' ability to successfully navigate terrain transitions by enforcing learned crossing events, significantly improving performance in obstacle-rich environments.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: A collision-free detour can still bring a legged robot to the next stair or ledge a few centimetres or degrees off, and a fixed locomotion skill, factory or learned, can stall or fall. Existing methods prevent this with a robot model or extensive trial and error, but on a new site with unknown skills neither is available, so they cannot be used. We find that a single 27-minute teaching session already supplies what these methods have to derive or learn: for every stair and ledge, one crossing the skill has completed. Our method, passage-conditioned navigation, makes the route remember how each transition was entered, not only where the path went. It stores each taught crossing as an event and, without training or a robot model, enforces it after every local replan: before each ledge, an entry gate makes the robot turn or back up and retry if it is more than 10 cm or 10° off the taught crossing. Under localization noise, with path, gait schedule, and sensing unchanged, this raises the share of disturbed ledge crossings that stay within these limits from 24.1% to 88.6%. In contact simulation with our learned policies, a robot pushed off course before stairs never falls in 180 climbs, against 9 falls when the stored direction is ignored; pushed 1.2 m away, it rejoins the route, ending on average 0.14 m from it (1.10 m without rejoining), and finishes as often as an undisturbed robot. This suits any robot with fixed skills that repeats a route over terrain transitions, as in inspection and patrol, where one wrong entry can end the task. We deployed it in competition on a real wheeled-legged robot: over 271 m of multi-obstacle terrain spanning 7.0 m of elevation, it completed all six runs, won third place at the 2026 Global Open-source AI Challenge, which drew 2,999 submissions, and was the only finalist in its task to finish fully autonomously.

机器人控制实验室.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Weile Gong, Zijian Lu, Jiahao Zheng, Bo Xu, Yiping Zuo
机器人控制实验室.summary: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC) optimizes embodied navigation by reducing model calls and inference time while maintaining effective performance through memory-guided adaptive reasoning.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

机器人控制实验室.title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yijun Liu, Shijia Ge, Tongtong Feng, Xin Wang, Yuan Meng
机器人控制实验室.summary: TwoPass introduces a self-conditioned framework for action-conditioned video prediction in robotic manipulation, achieving state-of-the-art results with significantly fewer network calls.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Action-conditioned video prediction lets robots anticipate the visual consequences of their actions for planning and policy evaluation. Existing predictors denoise each future from noise without using their own estimate of it, which limits the quality of the predicted future, in particular of the manipulated objects, and requires many network calls. We present TwoPass, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective. Self-Generated Draft Training supplies a detached clean-video estimate from the shared network as conditioning at the same noisy state. A Refinement-Only Late Adapter applies a dedicated residual transformation when a draft is present. At inference, Draft-Reuse Iterative Refinement obtains both a solver update and the next draft from each velocity prediction, requiring as few as 4 function evaluations (NFE) per video chunk. Training samples discrete solver-query noise levels and updates the pretrained backbone. Extensive experiments on Bridge and Language Table show that TwoPass achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors. Code: https://github.com/PlantPotatoOnMoon/TwoPass.

机器人控制实验室.title: VisualTalk-Bench: Evaluating Question-Driven Avatar-Led Video Explanations
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Xin Zhang, Tujie Xu, Zhiyi Chen, Xiaodong Zhang, Sicheng Yang
机器人控制实验室.summary: VisualTalk-Bench evaluates avatar-led video explanations for user questions, highlighting challenges in gesture alignment and establishing benchmarks for content accuracy and visual consistency.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Advances in video generation and avatar synthesis enable new ways to answer user questions through visual explanations. This task requires a system to formulate a correct answer, translate relevant information into visual material, and deliver the explanation through an avatar's speech and actions. Existing benchmarks rarely assess whether avatars point to the visual content being discussed. We introduce VisualTalk-Bench for question-driven avatar-led video explanations in finance and Chinese and English education. It includes 800 curated reference videos and 100 independent evaluation requests, assessing Content Factuality, Speech-Visual Consistency, Visual Quality, Motion Smoothness, and Avatar-Content Pointing. Yet end-to-end video generators often struggle to align gestures with specific visual targets. To explore this challenge, we develop Avatar-O Agent, a modular reference implementation with explicit interaction planning. Experiments across six agents show that factual precision and visual quality do not guarantee accurate pointing. A 26-participant study comparing four agents finds that Avatar-O Agent receives the highest average ratings for visual guidance, perceived pointing accuracy, and explanation effectiveness. We will release the data and code.

机器人控制实验室.title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Dijia Zhan, Jinyi Li, Xuemiao Xu, Yan Zhou, Yu Liu
机器人控制实验室.summary: RefreshGrad is an adaptive data-sampling method that enhances visuomotor learning by dynamically prioritizing informative trajectory segments during training, improving task success rates significantly.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies from demonstrations typically samples trajectory segments uniformly or relies on static offline data curation before training. However, we find that demonstration data vary sharply in supervision value across temporal windows, and that each window's value to the policy evolves substantially during training rather than being fixed or captured by raw loss alone. Motivated by this finding, we propose RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training. RefreshGrad focuses optimization on informative, learnable windows without altering the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost. Across ten LIBERO-Plus manipulation tasks, RefreshGrad boosts average success from 60.7% (Uniform) and 68.2% (FAKTUAL) to 76.1% under visual perturbations, and from 57.4% and 73.3% to 81.3% in clean scenes.

机器人控制实验室.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Hongyu Zhang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Heye Huang, Qingwen Meng, Wenjun Shi
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a planning framework that enhances trajectory selection for autonomous driving by integrating execution feedback and future representations to ensure road compliance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

机器人控制实验室.title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jinhao Zhang, Yushen Zuo, Ke Rui, Weitao Zhou, Haibao Yu
机器人控制实验室.summary: CoT-WAM is a novel framework that integrates vision-language models and world action models for enhanced semantic competence and predictive capabilities in robot manipulation tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. CoT-WAM uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information. A tailored two-stage training strategy enables joint optimization and more effective collaboration between the VLM and WAM. We evaluate CoT-WAM on six benchmarks covering control performance, zero-shot generalization, and long-horizon planning. CoT-WAM achieves SOTA performance on LIBERO, CALVIN, and RoboCasa-Kitchen, and demonstrates stronger zero-shot generalization on LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Pro without fine-tuning. On RoboCasa365, it further improves long-horizon planning over baselines with and without external planners. Real-world experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in practical deployments. Code is available at: https://github.com/jhz1192/CoT-WAM.git

机器人控制实验室.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Run Wang, Liang Wu, Ján Drgoňa, Yilin Mo
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents an action-affine world model for efficient refinement of frozen imitation policies, achieving high success rates with minimal latency in manipulation tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Imitation policies can fail through compounding errors, while existing refinement methods often require additional on-policy learning or expensive online planning. Our key insight is to model the response to small corrections around a policy proposal in an affine form that enables fast optimization. We refine a frozen imitation policy using an \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM), trained offline from perturbed policy rollouts. Conditioned on history and the proposal, the model directly predicts a nominal trajectory and a linear action response over the full horizon. With quadratic costs and linear constraints, refinement becomes a cheap quadratic program (QP), requiring only one model evaluation and one QP solve per control step. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to combine an action-affine world model with QP-based inference-time refinement of frozen imitation policies. Across four manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 4.2 ms of mean refinement latency per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

机器人控制实验室.title: Orchestrating Wheeled Mobile Robots Online without Conflicts
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jianghong Dong, Yifeng Zhang, Wenhan Cao, Jiawei Wang, Mengchi Cai
机器人控制实验室.summary: The CFOO framework enables wheeled mobile robots to adaptively navigate and maintain conflict-free formations in real-time, enhancing coordination and responsiveness to dynamic environments.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Formation control of wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) has been widely studied due to its broad applications. However, existing studies primarily focus on tracking predefined formations, with limited adaptability to varying environments. To address this limitation, we propose CFOO, a Conflict-Free Online Orchestration framework for continuous formation navigation of WMRs that integrates centralized formation generation with distributed formation maintenance. The upper layer monitors the environment in real time and generates adaptive formations as needed, using the proposed TCF-R2T (Trajectory-Conflict-Free Robot-to-Target assignment) algorithm to compute optimal assignments in polynomial time for timely, conflict-free formation transitions. At the lower layer, each WMR continuously employs JSTP (Joint Spatio-Temporal trajectory Planning) to maintain the given formation by jointly optimizing spatial positions and segment durations, improving coordination over spatial-only optimization with fixed durations. By coordinating these two layers, CFOO orchestrates WMRs to adapt their formations to varying environments and thus enable continuous navigation. Moreover, we design a Time-Varying Formation Reference (TVFR) mechanism to facilitate smooth transitions between successive desired formations. Both simulation and real-world experiments validate the effectiveness and adaptability of CFOO. Experimental videos are available on our project website: https://dongjh20.github.io/CFOO.

机器人控制实验室.title: Agent-Centric Observation Adaptation for Robust Visual Control under Dynamic Perturbations
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zhengru Fang, Yu Guo, Huanhuan Lou, Fei Liu, Yuang Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents ACO-MoE, a method enhancing visual control robustness under dynamic perturbations, achieving significant performance improvements in robotic tasks despite environmental challenges.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Visual control maps visual streams to actions in reinforcement learning and vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Changing weather, noise, blur, and compression can obscure different task cues within one episode. Existing control benchmarks mainly test scene distractions, while generic restorers optimize whole-image fidelity. We introduce the Visual Degraded Control Suite (VDCS) to evaluate seven degradations under Markov switching. We propose Agent-Centric Observations with Mixture-of-Experts (ACO-MoE), which routes each frame to a repair expert, restores RGB content, and composes task-relevant foregrounds. On eight VDCS tasks, corruption lowers DreamerV3's mean return from 769 to 562. ACO-MoE raises it to 730, recovering 81.2% of the lost return. It also improves returns on DMC-GB and RoboSuite and retains 70% to 97% of clean-input mean return under six unseen perturbation families. We train ACO-MoE on robot demonstrations and deploy it with a 3B-parameter VLA policy on a Piper arm for cube placement in blue and white boxes and cup placement on a coaster. On the blue-box and cup tasks, motion blur and physical low light with added noise reduce success from 100% to at most 10%. ACO-MoE raises success to 75% to 95% over 20 trials per task and condition.

机器人控制实验室.title: Breaking the Discretization Barrier of Continuous Physics Simulation Learning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Nan Wang, Lilan Peng, Kun Wang
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces CoPS, a data-driven approach that overcomes discretization limitations in continuous physics simulation learning by utilizing multiplicative filter networks and multi-scale graph ODEs.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: The modeling of complicated time-evolving physical dynamics from partial observations is a long-standing challenge. Particularly, observations can be sparsely distributed in a seemingly random or unstructured manner, making it difficult to capture highly nonlinear features in a variety of scientific and engineering problems. However, existing data-driven approaches are often constrained by fixed spatial and temporal discretization. While some researchers attempt to achieve spatio-temporal continuity by designing novel strategies, they either overly rely on traditional numerical methods or fail to truly overcome the limitations imposed by discretization. To address these, we propose CoPS, a purely data-driven methods, to effectively model continuous physics simulation from partial observations. Specifically, we employ multiplicative filter network to fuse and encode spatial information with the corresponding observations. Then we customize geometric grids and use message-passing mechanism to map features from original spatial domain to the customized grids. Subsequently, CoPS models continuous-time dynamics by designing multi-scale graph ODEs, while introducing a Markov-based neural auto-correction module to assist and constrain the continuous extrapolations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CoPS advances the state-of-the-art methods in space-time continuous modeling across various scenarios.

MMLab@NTU.title: MyoChallenge 2025: A New Benchmark for Human Athletic Intelligence
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Cheryl Wang, Chun Kwang Tan, Balint K. Hodossy, Eric Lyu, Jun Guo
MMLab@NTU.summary: MyoChallenge 2025 establishes a benchmark for athletic motor intelligence, combining musculoskeletal models and machine learning to enhance robotic performance in sports tasks.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Athletic performance represents the pinnacle of human motor intelligence, demanding rapid choices, precise control, agility, and coordinated physical execution. Replicating this seamless combination of capabilities remains elusive in current artificial intelligence and robotic systems. Concurrently, understanding the biological mastery of these movements is hindered because complex muscle coordination is rarely measured in vivo due to the limitations of physical equipment. To bridge this fundamental gap in understanding, MyoChallenge at NeurIPS 2025 established a pioneering benchmark for motor control intelligence in sports, leveraging high-fidelity musculoskeletal models within physics simulation combined with machine learning-driven algorithms. The competition introduces two distinct tracks emphasizing either upper or lower limbs control: a table tennis rally task utilizing a biomechanic upper limb composed of an arm with a hand and a trunk; and a soccer penalty kick using a biomechanic model of legs and a trunk. Marking the fourth iteration of the MyoChallenge series, this event attracted almost 70 teams and over 560 submissions globally, uniting a diverse community ranging from physicians and neuroscientists to machine learning experts. The competition facilitated the development of several state-of-the-art control algorithms for a musculoskeletal system capable of sports agility, leveraging techniques such as physics-based motion planners, on-policy behaviour cloning, hierarchical planning, and muscle synergies. By integrating standardized tasks and physiologically realistic models into the open-source framework of MyoSuite, MyoChallenge'25 serves as a reproducible and reusable testbed to accelerate interdisciplinary research across machine learning, biomechanics, sports science, and neuroscience. Project page: https://www.myosuite.org//myochallenge/myochallenge-2025.

MMLab@NTU.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Hangwei Zhang, Rujing Dang, Ruimin Lin, Jiahong Wu, Xiangxiang Chu
MMLab@NTU.summary: Plan4D introduces a generative model for 4D world prediction, enhancing visual fidelity and geometric accuracy by integrating video generation and 3D reconstruction techniques.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Specifically, we propose a model-stitching architecture that couples Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and augments it with an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The resulting model allows us to plan and generate complex, long-horizon, and fine-grained actions in a dynamic 3D scenes, while substantially improving both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy of the generated future videos. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. Project Page: https://fogradio.github.io/plan4d-project

MMLab@NTU.title: Composable Driving Style for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Guantian Zheng, Lidong Yu, Tianyu Gao, Jiashu Li, Jiaxing Chen
MMLab@NTU.summary: YOUDrive enables composable control of driving styles in end-to-end autonomous driving through a vision-language-action planner that adjusts behavior via learned task vectors.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. We propose YOUDrive, a vision--language--action planner for continuous and composable driving-style control. Each teacher's behavior is distilled into a task vector, a learned parameter update that induces a style direction in the planner's representation. These directions can be scaled and combined at inference without retraining the backbone. Conditioned on these directions, a flow-matching decoder models a multimodal trajectory distribution and generates kinematically feasible motion alternatives. We introduce the Style Alignment Score (SAS) to describe human-referenced kinematic behavior after safety and task gating. On NAVSIM navtest, a single coefficient monotonically controls assertiveness across six teacher-derived personas, while PDMS remains above 0.90 across the tested individual and blended configurations, reaching 0.954. Further analyses reveal systematic policy-specific kinematics after controlling for scene context, whereas the evaluated discrete style labels provide limited additional explanatory power. Code, checkpoints, and the metric will be released.

MMLab@NTU.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Kaiwen Zhang, Yiming Gao, Zeqi Xiao, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan
MMLab@NTU.summary: ViDecide introduces a decision-centric framework for training video diffusion models, enhancing multi-step reasoning and planning capabilities, achieving significant performance improvements over existing methods.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

MMLab@NTU.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Zichen Zhu, Dingye Liu, Nan Jiang, Danyang Zhang, Hang Zheng
MMLab@NTU.summary: SynthDCB is a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, utilizing world distillation to evaluate agent performance across diverse tasks and devices.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both interactive worlds and the tasks agents must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation (WD). World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone with 114 device classes, 1,166 functions, and 95 events, supporting five task families with 32 subtypes. Explicit states and tool-call traces support task validation and agent evaluation. We evaluate 22 models on 2,560 test tasks; the best achieves 88.8% mean Pass@1. Construction experiments demonstrate token efficiency and expansion of task coverage. At the richest knowledge level, WD fully covers 22/23 properties, 19/29 functionalities, and 30/39 event requirements specified in a real RobotVacuum protocol. Furthermore, the 1,000 sampled tasks semantically cover 81.6% of the 854 reference instructions in the real-world corpus. SynthDCB connects an expanding space of real-to-sim executable capabilities to verifiable agent evaluation.

MMLab@NTU.title: RAVEL: Asynchronous Rolling Inference for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Yuhan Chen, Ke Yu, Pengfei Liu, Shuxun Wang, Yi Yang
MMLab@NTU.summary: RAVEL introduces an asynchronous framework that reduces latency in flow-based vision-language-action models, enhancing robot responsiveness in dynamic environments while maintaining task performance.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models are highly effective for generalist robot manipulation, yet their reliance on computationally expensive VLM encoding and multi-step iterative action generation imposes a significant latency bottleneck. The resulting inference latency makes it difficult for robots to respond quickly, especially in dynamic environments. We address this limitation with RAVEL (Rolling Asynchronous VLA Enabling Low-Latency Control), an asynchronous inference framework that addresses the computational bottlenecks of both the VLM backbone and the action expert. To reduce the delay from multi-step action denoising, RAVEL allows near-term actions to be executed after a single additional denoising step by carrying partially denoised future actions forward in a rolling buffer. To avoid blocking on slow VLM encoding, RAVEL decouples VLM encoding from rolling action generation, allowing the action expert to operate continuously using the latest available VLM context, while a lightweight Fast Observation Pathway (FOP) directly conditions the action expert on current observations. Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, RAVEL consistently achieves substantially lower response latency while maintaining the task capability of the underlying VLA, enabling high-frequency and responsive closed-loop control.

MMLab@NTU.title: RoboForge: Cross-space Motion Refinement for Physically Executable Humanoid Whole-body Tracking
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Xichen Yuan, Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Xinying Guo
MMLab@NTU.summary: RoboForge enhances humanoid robot motion tracking by refining motion references through a data-centric framework, improving tracking success rates and enabling complex dynamic movements.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Whole-body motion tracking has rapidly expanded the skill repertoire of humanoid robots, yet nearly all of this progress has come from stronger tracking policies, while the motion references they imitate are treated as fixed supervision. We argue that reference quality is a first-order factor in tracking performance. Human motion data carry capture and estimation artifacts, and retargeting adds physical inconsistencies due to the human-robot embodiment gap; discarding such motions sacrifices valuable skill content, whereas retaining them uncorrected undermines policy learning. We present RoboForge, a data-centric framework that resolves this dilemma by refining references instead of filtering them, repairing each error in the space where it arises. In human motion space, a quality-guided diffusion model localizes corrupted segments and inpaints only those segments, leaving the rest of the motion intact. In robot motion space, kinematic repair corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects, and annealed sampling-based optimization under physics rollouts turns kinematically plausible references into dynamically executable ones. RoboForge requires no change to the tracker: it improves three retargeting methods and four tracking policies, raising the success rate of BeyondMimic from 89.51% to 96.20% while reducing the mean per-joint position error (MPJPE-L) by 31.6%. Refined references also accelerate policy learning, restore tracking performance from heavily corrupted inputs, and enable more than 30 high-dynamic motions, including flips and the Thomas flare, on a real Unitree G1.

MMLab@NTU.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Yanjing Li, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang, Xianbin Cao, Yawei Li
MMLab@NTU.summary: The paper presents QL-VLM, a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation framework that enhances efficiency and accuracy in vision-language models by reducing computation costs while preserving reasoning quality.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Efficient chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs) requires reducing both intermediate reasoning steps and their execution cost. Latent CoT methods compress textual rationales into continuous thoughts, yet their full-precision (FP) models retain substantial storage and computation costs. Lowering numerical precision could reduce these remaining costs, yet direct quantization severely degrades reasoning accuracy, particularly with 4-bit weights and activations. Operator and perturbation analyses reveal key sensitivity and direction-dependent predictive effects of continuous-thought errors, motivating preservation of information retrieval and subsequent reasoning beyond reconstruction accuracy. We therefore introduce QL-VLM, a dynamics-aware Quantization framework for efficient Latent reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). First, Dynamics-Guided Quantization (DGQ) uses nonuniform codebooks that preserve rotary-key structure, mitigating quantization-induced distortion in vision-language information retrieval. Second, Dynamics-Preserving Distillation (DPD) aligns continuous thoughts, latent-query readouts, and predictions with a full-precision teacher, maintaining predictive consistency through subsequent low-precision reasoning. On ScienceQA-IMG with Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, 4-bit QL-VLM achieves 90.43% accuracy and improves baseline by 40.33%, with 16.64x fewer bit-operations and 6.40x lower measured latency than explicit CoT.

MMLab@NTU.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Xu Pan, Chubin Zhang, Xingrui Yu, Runmin Lan, Zihao Wang
MMLab@NTU.summary: CauSyncVLA enhances asynchronous robot control by synchronizing perceptual memory with execution through a causal latent world model, achieving high success rates and improved motion smoothness.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

MMLab@NTU.title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Yichen Guo, Yanlong Chen, Xinyue Zhang, Mohan Liu, Song Zhang
MMLab@NTU.summary: The paper presents LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework for 4-bit world action models that enhances future prediction fidelity while maintaining performance and efficiency on robotic systems.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how a scene will evolve and condition their actions on this predicted future. Deploying them on a robot's onboard computer calls for 4-bit weights, activations and key-value caches (W4A4KV4). Existing 4-bit quantizers for WAMs preserve the generated action, and estimate sensitivity one denoising step at a time. However, they fail to preserve the fidelity of the predicted future: once the action pathway is protected, the remaining action error enters mostly through a degraded future that none of them deliberately protects. We propose LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read. Specifically, we introduce a reader metric, which measures future error by its effect on the action, and a read count, which weights each rounding error by the number of denoising steps that read it. Together they give the allocation of precision over activations and caches a closed-form solution. We further develop gaze-guided refinement, which gives the tokens the action attends to a second 4-bit pass in the denoising loop and in the cache. All weights stay at 4 bits, with no high-precision branch and no per-task recalibration. On the LIBERO-Plus benchmark, LAQ reaches 76.4% and 83.3% average success on Fast-WAM and Cosmos-Policy, within 1.2 percentage points of the 16-bit models and all above the baselines with 16-bit KV caches. It compresses the model by 3.8x, reduces the peak GPU memory of the whole policy by 2.3x, and runs 1.66x faster than the 16-bit model. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, it reaches 47.0% average success over three tasks, against 52.0% for the 16-bit model and 30.0% higher than QuaRot.

MMLab@NTU.title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Chenhao Wu, Zixiang Ni
MMLab@NTU.summary: This paper diagnoses failures in visual world-model planners as either search or scoring issues, proposing tailored remedies to improve planning outcomes across various environments.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

MMLab@NTU.title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Haoyun Tang, Baqiao Deng, Enjin Zhou, Songwen Tian, Keyao Xu
MMLab@NTU.summary: ThinkWAM enhances action refinement in world-action models through a bidirectional feedback loop, achieving high success rates across various robotic tasks without out-of-distribution fine-tuning.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk is identical for every proposal and thus carries no proposal-specific signal, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution. We introduce ThinkWAM, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop: the policy first proposes a complete action chunk, the proposal corrects multi-horizon future latents through a learned residual, and the corrected latents are injected into a second pass of the same action head, which generates the executable chunk. An affordance-guided observation-action memory and a near-fine, far-coarse multi-horizon prediction scheme, both motivated by predictive coding, support this loop, and all prediction stays in latent space. ThinkWAM achieves 98.70% success on LIBERO, 84.76% on LIBERO-Plus without OOD fine-tuning, 85.75%/65.85% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean/Random, and 65.17% on RoboCasa24. ThinkWAM achieves 64.4% mean success across three real-world OOD conditions. The mean two-pass inference latency per action chunk is 153.48 ms on LIBERO, 164.61 ms on RoboTwin, and 101.2 ms on the Galaxea A1Z. Ablations show complementary gains from rethinking and affordance guidance. Diagnostics indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.

MMLab@NTU.title: When and How Much to Imagine: Adaptive Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Visual Spatial Reasoning
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Shoubin Yu, Yue Zhang, Zun Wang, Jaehong Yoon, Huaxiu Yao
MMLab@NTU.summary: This paper introduces AVIC, an adaptive framework that optimizes visual imagination in spatial reasoning by selectively invoking it based on evidence sufficiency, enhancing efficiency and accuracy.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: Despite rapid progress in MLLMs, visual spatial reasoning remains unreliable when correct answers depend on how a scene would appear under unseen or alternative viewpoints. Recent work addresses this by augmenting reasoning with world models for visual imagination, but questions such as when imagination is actually necessary, how much of it is beneficial, and when it becomes harmful, remain poorly understood. In practice, indiscriminate imagination can increase computation and even degrade performance by introducing misleading evidence. In this work, we present an in-depth analysis of test-time visual imagination as a controllable resource for spatial reasoning. We first study when static visual evidence is sufficient, when imagination improves reasoning, and how excessive or unnecessary imagination affects accuracy and efficiency. To support this analysis, we then introduce AVIC, an adaptive test-time framework with world models that explicitly reasons about the sufficiency of current visual evidence before selectively invoking and scaling visual imagination. Finally, to further learn this gating and planning behavior without any annotation of when and how much to imagine, we introduce AVIC-R, which trains the policy via GRPO from QA-correctness rewards and penalties by imagination cost. Across spatial reasoning benchmarks (SAT, MMSI) and an embodied navigation benchmark (R2R), our results reveal clear scenarios where imagination is critical, marginal, or detrimental, and show that selective control can match or outperform fixed imagination strategies with substantially fewer world-model calls and language tokens. Our AVIC-R surpasses strong proprietary baselines including GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 while invoking the world model less often. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of analyzing and controlling test-time imagination for efficient and reliable spatial reasoning.

MMLab@NTU.title: Breaking the Discretization Barrier of Continuous Physics Simulation Learning
MMLab@NTU.authors_text: Fan Xu, Hao Wu, Nan Wang, Lilan Peng, Kun Wang
MMLab@NTU.summary: The paper introduces CoPS, a data-driven approach that overcomes discretization limitations in continuous physics simulation learning by utilizing multiplicative filter networks and multi-scale graph ODEs.
MMLab@NTU.debug_abstract: The modeling of complicated time-evolving physical dynamics from partial observations is a long-standing challenge. Particularly, observations can be sparsely distributed in a seemingly random or unstructured manner, making it difficult to capture highly nonlinear features in a variety of scientific and engineering problems. However, existing data-driven approaches are often constrained by fixed spatial and temporal discretization. While some researchers attempt to achieve spatio-temporal continuity by designing novel strategies, they either overly rely on traditional numerical methods or fail to truly overcome the limitations imposed by discretization. To address these, we propose CoPS, a purely data-driven methods, to effectively model continuous physics simulation from partial observations. Specifically, we employ multiplicative filter network to fuse and encode spatial information with the corresponding observations. Then we customize geometric grids and use message-passing mechanism to map features from original spatial domain to the customized grids. Subsequently, CoPS models continuous-time dynamics by designing multi-scale graph ODEs, while introducing a Markov-based neural auto-correction module to assist and constrain the continuous extrapolations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CoPS advances the state-of-the-art methods in space-time continuous modeling across various scenarios.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Linjia Kang, Binhan Jiang, Juan Yang, Zhiqin Song, Xiangsen Wu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: StarTV-Agent enhances traffic scenario understanding by integrating policy learning and experience evolution, achieving improved performance and efficiency through adaptive reasoning and workflow reuse.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible.
