ReThinkLab.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Xingyi Wang, Bin Li, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Weiji Xie
ReThinkLab.summary: ECHO is an in-context behavior foundation model that enhances humanoid control by adapting general skills to specific environments through structured dynamics representation and residual corrections.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

ReThinkLab.title: DACA: Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Jiaming Liu, Linghe Kong, Guixu Zhang, Huaxi Huang
ReThinkLab.summary: The Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent (DACA) enhances zero-shot 3D visual grounding by integrating semantic and geometric reasoning for improved accuracy and autonomous decision-making.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: 3D visual grounding (3D-VG) is a task that bridges the natural language and 3D space, serving as a foundational capability for embodied intelligence and human-computer interaction. Although recent 3D-VG agents overcome the reliance on pre-processed 3D point clouds, they essentially employ a unidirectional, pipeline-style tool-calling architecture. This architecture separates semantic understanding from geometric reconstruction, leading to error accumulation and an inability to autonomously recover from failures. To address this flaw, this paper proposes the Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent (DACA), which reinterprets 3D-VG as a semantic-geometric dual-anchor collaborative reasoning paradigm. DACA comprises two complementary specialized tools: the semantic anchor tool holds the visual semantic features of the target and achieves efficient target tracking via optical flow and VLM local verification; the geometric anchor tool holds the 3D spatial geometric features of the target and performs global spatial reasoning via voxelization and multi-keypoint projection. The two components exchange information bidirectionally via a standardized tool call protocol, autonomously deciding on the next perception-action step to form a closed-loop optimization. Experiments on the ScanRefer and Nr3D benchmarks demonstrate that zero-shot DACA achieves an overall Acc@0.25 of 73.6\% on ScanRefer and 70.4\% overall accuracy on Nr3D, far surpassing the latest zero-shot 3D-VG methods. The code and models are available at https://github.com/liujia99/DACA

ReThinkLab.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zichen Zhu, Dingye Liu, Nan Jiang, Danyang Zhang, Hang Zheng
ReThinkLab.summary: SynthDCB is a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, utilizing world distillation to evaluate agent performance across diverse tasks and devices.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both interactive worlds and the tasks agents must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation (WD). World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone with 114 device classes, 1,166 functions, and 95 events, supporting five task families with 32 subtypes. Explicit states and tool-call traces support task validation and agent evaluation. We evaluate 22 models on 2,560 test tasks; the best achieves 88.8% mean Pass@1. Construction experiments demonstrate token efficiency and expansion of task coverage. At the richest knowledge level, WD fully covers 22/23 properties, 19/29 functionalities, and 30/39 event requirements specified in a real RobotVacuum protocol. Furthermore, the 1,000 sampled tasks semantically cover 81.6% of the 854 reference instructions in the real-world corpus. SynthDCB connects an expanding space of real-to-sim executable capabilities to verifiable agent evaluation.

ReThinkLab.title: GLoTouch: Global-to-Local Haptic Perception Using a Parallel Gripper for Object Search, Recognition, and Grasping Without External Vision
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zonglin Li, Wanruo Zhang, Yiming Wang, Kun Song, Xinyi Zhou
ReThinkLab.summary: GLoTouch is a novel haptic perception framework enabling parallel grippers to perform object search, recognition, and grasping in low-light conditions without external vision.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Perceiving objects in the environment is a fundamental capability of autonomous robots. In dark or low-light environments, external cameras often fail to reliably perceive object positions and geometry; when visual sensing is unavailable, completing target search, recognition, and grasping through touch alone becomes a key robot manipulation capability. This task must simultaneously address container-scale spatial exploration and object-scale fine-grained geometric perception, which is particularly challenging for low-degree-of-freedom parallel grippers. However, a unified framework remains lacking for connecting container-scale spatial exploration with object-scale fine-grained geometric perception and grasping. To address this challenge, we present \textbf{GLoTouch}, a global-to-local haptic perception and manipulation framework built on a parallel gripper. In the global stage, the gripper holds a passive long-reach probe, combining force measurements with known tool geometry to localize contacts and actively estimate candidate-object positions, coarse contours, and heights. In the local stage, the robot sets down the probe and uses the bilateral visuotactile sensors on the same gripper to directly acquire local haptic observations, which are matched against a given target 3-D model without object-specific training. We evaluate the framework in both simulation and real-robot experiments. Source code will be open-sourced.

赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: 3D visual grounding (3D-VG) is a task that bridges the natural language and 3D space, serving as a foundational capability for embodied intelligence and human-computer interaction. Although recent 3D-VG agents overcome the reliance on pre-processed 3D point clouds, they essentially employ a unidirectional, pipeline-style tool-calling architecture. This architecture separates semantic understanding from geometric reconstruction, leading to error accumulation and an inability to autonomously recover from failures. To address this flaw, this paper proposes the Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent (DACA), which reinterprets 3D-VG as a semantic-geometric dual-anchor collaborative reasoning paradigm. DACA comprises two complementary specialized tools: the semantic anchor tool holds the visual semantic features of the target and achieves efficient target tracking via optical flow and VLM local verification; the geometric anchor tool holds the 3D spatial geometric features of the target and performs global spatial reasoning via voxelization and multi-keypoint projection. The two components exchange information bidirectionally via a standardized tool call protocol, autonomously deciding on the next perception-action step to form a closed-loop optimization. Experiments on the ScanRefer and Nr3D benchmarks demonstrate that zero-shot DACA achieves an overall Acc@0.25 of 73.6\% on ScanRefer and 70.4\% overall accuracy on Nr3D, far surpassing the latest zero-shot 3D-VG methods. The code and models are available at https://github.com/liujia99/DACA

赵波老师实验室.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Zichen Zhu, Dingye Liu, Nan Jiang, Danyang Zhang, Hang Zheng
赵波老师实验室.summary: SynthDCB is a scalable benchmark for device control and environment awareness, utilizing world distillation to evaluate agent performance across diverse tasks and devices.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both interactive worlds and the tasks agents must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation (WD). World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone with 114 device classes, 1,166 functions, and 95 events, supporting five task families with 32 subtypes. Explicit states and tool-call traces support task validation and agent evaluation. We evaluate 22 models on 2,560 test tasks; the best achieves 88.8% mean Pass@1. Construction experiments demonstrate token efficiency and expansion of task coverage. At the richest knowledge level, WD fully covers 22/23 properties, 19/29 functionalities, and 30/39 event requirements specified in a real RobotVacuum protocol. Furthermore, the 1,000 sampled tasks semantically cover 81.6% of the 854 reference instructions in the real-world corpus. SynthDCB connects an expanding space of real-to-sim executable capabilities to verifiable agent evaluation.

赵波老师实验室.title: GLoTouch: Global-to-Local Haptic Perception Using a Parallel Gripper for Object Search, Recognition, and Grasping Without External Vision
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Zonglin Li, Wanruo Zhang, Yiming Wang, Kun Song, Xinyi Zhou
赵波老师实验室.summary: GLoTouch is a novel haptic perception framework enabling parallel grippers to perform object search, recognition, and grasping in low-light conditions without external vision.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Perceiving objects in the environment is a fundamental capability of autonomous robots. In dark or low-light environments, external cameras often fail to reliably perceive object positions and geometry; when visual sensing is unavailable, completing target search, recognition, and grasping through touch alone becomes a key robot manipulation capability. This task must simultaneously address container-scale spatial exploration and object-scale fine-grained geometric perception, which is particularly challenging for low-degree-of-freedom parallel grippers. However, a unified framework remains lacking for connecting container-scale spatial exploration with object-scale fine-grained geometric perception and grasping. To address this challenge, we present \textbf{GLoTouch}, a global-to-local haptic perception and manipulation framework built on a parallel gripper. In the global stage, the gripper holds a passive long-reach probe, combining force measurements with known tool geometry to localize contacts and actively estimate candidate-object positions, coarse contours, and heights. In the local stage, the robot sets down the probe and uses the bilateral visuotactile sensors on the same gripper to directly acquire local haptic observations, which are matched against a given target 3-D model without object-specific training. We evaluate the framework in both simulation and real-robot experiments. Source code will be open-sourced.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Chengyang Dong, Ze Chen, Kai Ye, Chutian Wang, Heng Xu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: Dune is a novel zeroth-order optimizer that enhances test-time adaptation for VLA models by integrating historical error prediction to reduce estimation variance and improve stability.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to handle distribution shifts during deployment without source-domain retraining. However, backpropagation-based adaptation incurs heavy memory overhead on resource-constrained robots, whereas zeroth-order (ZO) methods suffer from high estimation variance under limited perturbation budgets. We observe that while ZO estimation enables low-memory adaptation with rapid initial gains, it often stalls or degrades over long-horizon updates due to noisy gradient estimates. To address these limitations, we propose Dune, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations. Specifically, Dune learns a lightweight, time-conditioned error predictor from past optimization dynamics and fuses its predictions with instantaneous ZO estimates, achieving effective variance reduction without backpropagation or extra forward passes. Additionally, we theoretically characterize how estimation variance restricts convergence in high-dimensional, small-population regimes, motivating the use of historical statistics. Extensive experiments on LIBERO and real-world robots demonstrate that Dune achieves superior success rates under a low memory footprint, with ablations confirming improved closed-loop stability and post-disturbance recovery.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Evo-DexBench: Benchmarking Generalization across Related Tasks for Dexterous Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Bing Cheng, Yiran Mao, Zewei Ye, Yifan Jin, Xinyi Chen
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: Evo-DexBench introduces a controlled benchmark for evaluating dexterous manipulation policies' ability to generalize knowledge transfer across related tasks with limited demonstrations.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: General-purpose dexterous manipulation requires policies to transfer knowledge from related tasks to new tasks with only a few target demonstrations. Existing benchmarks often provide too many target demonstrations and leave the differences between source and target tasks uncontrolled. As a result, they cannot clearly distinguish knowledge transfer from task memorization. Our key insight is the Core-Gen principle. Core tasks are related tasks that share a functional interaction and provide source knowledge, while a Gen task is a novel target within the same functional family that has only a few demonstrations. This setup tests whether a policy can reuse functional interaction knowledge. Based on this principle, we propose Evo-DexBench, which controls both source-task relatedness and target-task exposure. It comprises 30 tasks in six functional families, three everyday layouts per task, and 1,248 multimodal demonstrations collected via VR teleoperation with simulated Shadow Hands equipped with 123 taxels. We first compare few-shot adaptation strategies and find that joint Core + Gen training makes the most effective use of Core knowledge. Under this setting, we evaluate six representative policies. The best-performing policy, $π_{0.5}$, achieves a mean success rate of only 24.4%, revealing the limitations of existing methods in transferring functional interaction knowledge. Further analysis shows that on the tested Gen targets, functionally matched Core data yields larger success-rate gains than mismatched data, and that with matched Core data, 8 Gen demonstrations reach the performance of training on 16--32 Gen demonstrations alone. These results indicate that Evo-DexBench separates knowledge transfer from task memorization under controlled conditions and effectively evaluates the generalization of dexterous manipulation policies across related tasks.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Bridging Time and Space: Decoupled Spatio-Temporal Alignment for Video Grounding
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xuezhen Tu, Jingyu Wu, Fangyu Kang, Qingpeng Nong, Kaijin Zhang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: The paper presents Bridge-STG, an innovative framework that decouples spatio-temporal alignment for video grounding, enhancing performance by addressing token redundancy and semantic coherence.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding requires jointly localizing target objects across both temporal and spatial dimensions based on natural language queries, posing fundamental challenges for existing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). We identify two core challenges: \textit{entangled spatio-temporal alignment}, arising from coupling two heterogeneous sub-tasks within the same autoregressive output space, and \textit{dual-domain visual token redundancy}, where target objects exhibit simultaneous temporal and spatial sparsity, rendering the overwhelming majority of visual tokens irrelevant to the grounding query. To address these, we propose \textbf{Bridge-STG}, an end-to-end framework that decouples temporal and spatial localization while maintaining semantic coherence. While decoupling is the natural solution to this entanglement, it risks creating a semantic gap between the temporal MLLM and the spatial decoder. Bridge-STG resolves this through two pivotal designs: the \textbf{Spatio-Temporal Semantic Bridging (STSB)} mechanism with Explicit Temporal Alignment (ETA) distills the MLLM's temporal reasoning context into enriched bridging queries as a robust semantic interface; and the \textbf{Query-Guided Spatial Localization (QGSL)} module leverages these queries to drive a purpose-built spatial decoder with multi-layer interactive queries and positive/negative frame sampling, jointly eliminating dual-domain visual token redundancy. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that Bridge-STG achieves state-of-the-art performance among MLLM-based methods. Bridge-STG improves average m\_vIoU from $26.4$ to $34.3$ on VidSTG and demonstrates strong cross-task transfer across various fine-grained video understanding tasks under a unified multi-task training regime.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xuyang Liu, Chenwen Lu, Junxi Wang, Siyu Ren, Xinying Lin
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: MemFolder introduces a structure-guided memory folding framework that efficiently reduces record count and context length in agent memory management, enhancing performance retention while minimizing storage costs.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Long-term agents accumulate large external memory stores as interactions unfold, increasing the costs of storage, retrieval, and response generation. Efficiency is constrained by two coupled factors: a growing record count increases retrieval overhead, while longer retrieved contexts increase prefill computation and decoding-time attention costs. Existing methods prune or consolidate records, but pruning can discard useful evidence, whereas consolidation may produce fewer yet longer retrieval units. We introduce MemFolder, a structure-guided memory folding framework that sequentially reduces record count and context length. The framework comprises two core components that share memory groups, using cross-record structure to guide both evidence consolidation and compact representation. RecordFolder grounds entity mentions, progressively selects representative yet complementary anchors, and combines semantic and entity affinity with temporal chaining to consolidate compatible records into fewer retrieval units. ContextFolder encodes the original records within these groups into compact text and uses verification feedback to revise encodings when key facts cannot be recovered. Experiments on the three text-based memory benchmarks LoCoMo, PersonaMem, and LongMemEval and the two multimodal benchmarks M3-Bench-web and M3-Bench-robot demonstrate the strong performance of our methods. Notably, on Mem0, RecordFolder retains 99.0% of the original average performance across the three text-based benchmarks with 50% fewer records, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.9 percentage points in performance retention. Combined with ContextFolder, existing record compression methods further shorten their output records while retaining most of their performance.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xingyi Wang, Bin Li, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Weiji Xie
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: ECHO is an in-context behavior foundation model that enhances humanoid control by adapting general skills to specific environments through structured dynamics representation and residual corrections.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: GLoTouch: Global-to-Local Haptic Perception Using a Parallel Gripper for Object Search, Recognition, and Grasping Without External Vision
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zonglin Li, Wanruo Zhang, Yiming Wang, Kun Song, Xinyi Zhou
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: GLoTouch is a novel haptic perception framework enabling parallel grippers to perform object search, recognition, and grasping in low-light conditions without external vision.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Perceiving objects in the environment is a fundamental capability of autonomous robots. In dark or low-light environments, external cameras often fail to reliably perceive object positions and geometry; when visual sensing is unavailable, completing target search, recognition, and grasping through touch alone becomes a key robot manipulation capability. This task must simultaneously address container-scale spatial exploration and object-scale fine-grained geometric perception, which is particularly challenging for low-degree-of-freedom parallel grippers. However, a unified framework remains lacking for connecting container-scale spatial exploration with object-scale fine-grained geometric perception and grasping. To address this challenge, we present \textbf{GLoTouch}, a global-to-local haptic perception and manipulation framework built on a parallel gripper. In the global stage, the gripper holds a passive long-reach probe, combining force measurements with known tool geometry to localize contacts and actively estimate candidate-object positions, coarse contours, and heights. In the local stage, the robot sets down the probe and uses the bilateral visuotactile sensors on the same gripper to directly acquire local haptic observations, which are matched against a given target 3-D model without object-specific training. We evaluate the framework in both simulation and real-robot experiments. Source code will be open-sourced.

北京航空航天大学.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
北京航空航天大学.summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

北京航空航天大学.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Yanjing Li, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang, Xianbin Cao, Yawei Li
北京航空航天大学.summary: The paper presents QL-VLM, a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation framework that enhances efficiency and accuracy in vision-language models by reducing computation costs while preserving reasoning quality.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Efficient chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs) requires reducing both intermediate reasoning steps and their execution cost. Latent CoT methods compress textual rationales into continuous thoughts, yet their full-precision (FP) models retain substantial storage and computation costs. Lowering numerical precision could reduce these remaining costs, yet direct quantization severely degrades reasoning accuracy, particularly with 4-bit weights and activations. Operator and perturbation analyses reveal key sensitivity and direction-dependent predictive effects of continuous-thought errors, motivating preservation of information retrieval and subsequent reasoning beyond reconstruction accuracy. We therefore introduce QL-VLM, a dynamics-aware Quantization framework for efficient Latent reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs). First, Dynamics-Guided Quantization (DGQ) uses nonuniform codebooks that preserve rotary-key structure, mitigating quantization-induced distortion in vision-language information retrieval. Second, Dynamics-Preserving Distillation (DPD) aligns continuous thoughts, latent-query readouts, and predictions with a full-precision teacher, maintaining predictive consistency through subsequent low-precision reasoning. On ScienceQA-IMG with Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, 4-bit QL-VLM achieves 90.43% accuracy and improves baseline by 40.33%, with 16.64x fewer bit-operations and 6.40x lower measured latency than explicit CoT.

北京航空航天大学.title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Xinze Shi, Litian Zhang, Zhenjie Su, Zelong Yu, Yuting Zhang
北京航空航天大学.summary: The Bradley-Terry training objective can significantly distort outcome probabilities in language world models, leading to inaccurate predictions despite initial accuracy.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Comparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes. We show that, fitted with a Bradley-Terry objective, it need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. On a simulated robot push with enumerated outcome distributions, this objective takes a model that is accurate on unseen layouts (hazard error 2.4 percentage points, pp) and moves 33 to 43 pp of its probability onto outcomes that none of a condition's enumerated branches produces. The cause is the objective, not the comparisons: its optimum, computed before training, predicts where the model ends up, and a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without the shift. The shift is robust: it recurs on unseen conditions, under five candidate laws and a three-fold denser enumeration, and about 29 pp remain without the physically impossible events. Its cost is conditional: with those events it inflates hazard probabilities, and a threshold inherited from the pre-feedback model costs about 3 pp of utility per decision on trained and 1 to 2 pp on unseen conditions, through false rejects; without them the utility loss averages below 1 pp over six seeds, though a small regret in action choice remains. Audits of readout, response and decision trace the effect from probabilities to actions.

北京航空航天大学.title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Linfeng Dong, Jianwei Niu, Jiuyi Zhao, Ruibing Feng, Xinghao Wu
北京航空航天大学.summary: ActMem introduces a novel in-context memory framework that enhances Vision-Language-Action models by decoupling memory reasoning from perception, achieving superior task success rates in robotic manipulation.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role. However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena, surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.

北京航空航天大学.title: UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Mengkun Liang, Haoran Qiang, Guannan Liu, Junjie Wu
北京航空航天大学.summary: UpliftMem enhances agent memory retrieval by learning set-level execution uplift, improving decision accuracy significantly through targeted probing and closed-form expected value criteria.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents draw on external memory to guide new tasks, raising the question of which memories to retrieve together to improve execution. Learning set values requires outcome feedback, but evaluating each untested alternative costs an additional rollout. We introduce \textsc{UpliftMem}, which learns set-level execution uplift relative to the same executor without memory. Our analysis of how retrieval preferences limit feedback coverage motivates targeted probes. Under a correlated Gaussian surrogate, we derive a closed-form expected value of sample information (EVSI) criterion that prioritizes probes by their expected benefit to local retrieval decisions. The feedback trains a shared scorer with the executor frozen, and inference requires no probing. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and BigCodeBench, \textsc{UpliftMem} achieves best or joint-best success rates among evaluated methods. On fixed-store MemSyco-Bench evaluations, decision accuracy increases from 41.7\% to 66.5\% with Qwen3-4B and from 44.4\% to 68.8\% with Qwen3-8B. At matched probe budgets, EVSI improves decision accuracy over random probing by 10.6 and 13.9 percentage points, respectively.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
