HMI Lab.title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
HMI Lab.authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Chenhao Wu, Zixiang Ni
HMI Lab.summary: This paper diagnoses failures in visual world-model planners as either search or scoring issues, proposing tailored remedies to improve planning outcomes across various environments.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

HMI Lab.title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
HMI Lab.summary: This study investigates the impact of cross-view consistency on multi-view visual augmentation for visuomotor policies, revealing selective constraints on appearance and geometry for optimal performance.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiaming Li, Lingzhen Li, Xiaze Yang, Chenyu Zhu, Kaiqi Liu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: SpecWM introduces a training-free inference framework that enhances streaming world models by refining draft chunks through latent velocity verification, achieving improved visual quality and speed.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, enhancing immersive experiences and overcoming limitations of existing methods with innovative training techniques.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Wanyi Chen, Xiao Yang, Xu Yang, Tianming Sha, Qizheng Li
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench evaluates LLM agents' capabilities in autonomously engineering RL post-training pipelines, revealing both intelligent behaviors and significant limitations across various tasks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: We introduce Agent^2 RL-Bench, a compact diagnostic benchmark for evaluating agentic RL post-training, which tests whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and execute post-training pipelines that improve foundation models. RL post-training increasingly drives model alignment and specialization, yet existing benchmarks are largely static, rewarding supervised fine-tuning or script generation without assessing an agent's ability to close an interactive RL loop. Agent^2 RL-Bench provides a unified agent-facing interface: each run starts from an isolated workspace containing a base model, task data, instructions, and a grading API, and agents must iterate within a fixed budget by training models and submitting artifacts for evaluation. The benchmark spans six tasks across three levels, from static rule-based training to judge-based optimization and closed-loop online RL with trajectory collection. Two diagnostic skills, namely runtime recording and post-hoc summarization, enable structured analysis of agent behavior, facilitating smooth and effective iteration of the benchmark's evaluation framework. Across five agent systems and six driver LLMs, agents show intelligent behavior but clear limitations: one RL-oriented run improves ALFWorld from 4.85 to 93.28 via SFT warm-up and GRPO with online rollouts, yet DeepSearchQA remains difficult, most successful routes rely on supervised pipelines, and interactive outcomes show large differences across agent stacks. Overall, Agent2 RL-Bench shows that current agents can sometimes engineer online RL, but stable agent-driven RL post-training remains rare under fixed budgets. It also demonstrates that our benchmark provides a strong and effective evaluation framework for future research in this direction. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Bo Li, Taoyong Cui, Bob Zhang, Mengran Li, Chengyang Zhang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: WeightCode introduces Weight-Space Programming to enhance neural networks' capabilities by directly modifying weights with executable programs, achieving significant performance improvements without retraining.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original command and navigation capabilities. On ImageNet, four weight programs achieve net gains of 8.84-17.62 points while preserving clean accuracy, outperforming the best of eight fine-tuning methods under matched examples, checks, and retention constraints. In a Vision Transformer, causal interventions show that installed noise-correction gates drive robustness gains, while their selective activation preserves clean accuracy. Rerun on five independently trained Vision Transformers without further language model calls, ten weight programs retain 83-110% of their source-network gains on average, whereas copying their fixed weight edits yields negligible gains. Six programs written for an already edited network add 5.23-14.50 points of contrast robustness while retaining the previously installed noise gain. Together, these results establish WSP as a new route to acquiring and accumulating capabilities in trained neural networks through reusable weight programs.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent framework that optimizes memory retention through local verification, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Haoran Ye, Yuxing Lu, Haonan Dong, Zhaochen Su, Guojie Song
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: Harness-Zero enables agent harness distillation by using an optimized harness to guide training, enhancing model performance and behavior recovery while eliminating the need for specialized harnesses at deployment.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: (1) For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness. (2) With the specialized harness removed at deployment, Harness-Zero improves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached, while reducing inference token usage by 27%-86%. (3) Harness-Zero recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Boyu Chen, Jiaqi Liang, Xini Ding
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: GroundingPI is a state-of-the-art grounding foundation model that enhances physical intelligence in robotics by improving object localization and manipulation through advanced multimodal training techniques.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: GroundAnything: Reconciling Parallel Decoding with Precise Visual Grounding at Flash Speed
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Bowen Ping, Xini Ding, Zetian Song
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: GroundAnything is a 4B-parameter model that achieves fast, precise visual grounding through parallel decoding and iterative denoising, outperforming existing models on multiple benchmarks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Autoregressive (AR) grounding models serialize spatial predictions, introducing sequential latency and imposing a causal order on output tokens. We view grounding as visual evidence extraction: objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query, yet their dependencies do not imply an intrinsic left-to-right generation order. This distinction makes bidirectional diffusion a natural fit, allowing spatial hypotheses to emerge in parallel and be jointly refined through iterative denoising. We introduce GroundAnything, a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model that reconciles fast parallel decoding with precise localization through blockwise denoising. Training combines grounding pretraining from public datasets and dedicated data engines, direct AR-to-diffusion conversion with joint AR and diffusion objectives, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO-based reinforcement post-training. Across 30 grounding benchmarks, our autoregressive variant, GroundAnything-VLM, establishes a new overall state of the art among similarly sized models at 72.42%, remaining competitive with GPT-6 Astra (71.35%). With entropy-guided decoding, GroundAnything also surpasses the prior state of the art at this scale, averaging 61.75% versus 53.32% for the fast MTP-based LocateAnything model. We further explore decoding strategies, showing that an optional self-speculative mode achieves a 4.51$\times$ speedup over the AR counterpart with a 0.74 percentage-point drop in COCO F1mIoU. Infrastructure experiments show that progressive inference optimizations translate parallel decoding into practical speedups. These gains support efficient visual grounding in latency-sensitive real-world systems.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: TacInno introduces a novel approach to enhance Vision-Language-Action models by using tactile innovation as a training target, significantly improving manipulation success rates.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Xu, Yifu Yuan
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: SpatialScout-V2 enhances active mapping in real 3D environments, revealing significant challenges in object localization accuracy among various vision-language models.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to acquire visual evidence and integrate partial observations into coherent three-dimensional representations. We introduce SpatialScout-V2, which extends SpatialScout's active mapping task from simulation to real residential scenes through three advances: real visual observations, preservation of original scene content, and interactive exploration of recorded views. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, the benchmark covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories. Given a fixed target inventory, agents autonomously select recorded viewpoints and viewing directions, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively estimate and revise object centers within a fixed interaction budget. We evaluate the localization accuracy and completeness of object-center maps using mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models (VLMs), we find that six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20\%. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches only 22.52\%, with just 18.36\% of targets exceeding an IoU of 0.5. Further analysis shows that broad submission coverage can coexist with limited localization accuracy, while target omissions further reduce overall scores. These results highlight substantial challenges in constructing accurate and complete object-center maps through active exploration of real scenes.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Bingqing Jiang, Guoxi Zhang, Jasper Wang, Bingning Wang, Difan Zou
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO) to enhance multimodal reasoning in vision-language models by assigning role-specific credit to perception and reasoning tokens.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), especially with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has shown strong potential for improving the reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs). However, in multimodal reasoning, final-answer rewards are typically assigned at the sequence level and do not distinguish the functional roles of different tokens, making it difficult to determine whether a correct answer is supported by task-relevant visual evidence. In this paper, we revisit multimodal RLVR from the perspective of role-aware token-level credit assignment, where structured responses are decomposed into perception tokens for extracting visual evidence and reasoning tokens for deriving answers from that evidence. Based on this perspective, we propose Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO), which refines the sequence-level GRPO advantage into role-aware token-level advantages without changing the reward function. Specifically, SRPO assigns role-specific credit by using self-distilled on-policy contrasts: perception tokens are emphasized according to their visual dependency under original versus corrupted visual inputs, while reasoning tokens are emphasized according to their consistency with the generated perception. These role-specific signals are further unified through a shared trajectory-level baseline, yielding positive token weights that adjust relative update magnitudes while preserving the original GRPO reward and advantage signs, without requiring external reward models or separate teachers. Experiments across diverse multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that SRPO improves evidence-grounded reasoning, highlighting the importance of moving beyond uniform sequence-level credit toward role-aware optimization for reliable multimodal reasoning.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: RoboForge: Cross-space Motion Refinement for Physically Executable Humanoid Whole-body Tracking
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Xichen Yuan, Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Xinying Guo
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: RoboForge enhances humanoid robot motion tracking by refining motion references through a data-centric framework, improving tracking success rates and enabling complex dynamic movements.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Whole-body motion tracking has rapidly expanded the skill repertoire of humanoid robots, yet nearly all of this progress has come from stronger tracking policies, while the motion references they imitate are treated as fixed supervision. We argue that reference quality is a first-order factor in tracking performance. Human motion data carry capture and estimation artifacts, and retargeting adds physical inconsistencies due to the human-robot embodiment gap; discarding such motions sacrifices valuable skill content, whereas retaining them uncorrected undermines policy learning. We present RoboForge, a data-centric framework that resolves this dilemma by refining references instead of filtering them, repairing each error in the space where it arises. In human motion space, a quality-guided diffusion model localizes corrupted segments and inpaints only those segments, leaving the rest of the motion intact. In robot motion space, kinematic repair corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects, and annealed sampling-based optimization under physics rollouts turns kinematically plausible references into dynamically executable ones. RoboForge requires no change to the tracker: it improves three retargeting methods and four tracking policies, raising the success rate of BeyondMimic from 89.51% to 96.20% while reducing the mean per-joint position error (MPJPE-L) by 31.6%. Refined references also accelerate policy learning, restore tracking performance from heavily corrupted inputs, and enable more than 30 high-dynamic motions, including flips and the Thomas flare, on a real Unitree G1.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Chenhao Wu, Zixiang Ni
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: This paper diagnoses failures in visual world-model planners as either search or scoring issues, proposing tailored remedies to improve planning outcomes across various environments.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: This study investigates the impact of cross-view consistency on multi-view visual augmentation for visuomotor policies, revealing selective constraints on appearance and geometry for optimal performance.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Shihan Wu, You Liu, Chunyu He, Minghui Qin, Longhan Jiao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: HumanCOIN is a comprehensive 12,500-hour dataset capturing human intent in egocentric manipulation through three observational tiers: gaze, muscle exertion, and cognitive decision-making.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiaming Li, Lingzhen Li, Xiaze Yang, Chenyu Zhu, Kaiqi Liu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SpecWM introduces a training-free inference framework that enhances streaming world models by refining draft chunks through latent velocity verification, achieving improved visual quality and speed.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded exocentric-to-egocentric video generation, enhancing immersive experiences and overcoming limitations of existing methods with innovative training techniques.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Wanyi Chen, Xiao Yang, Xu Yang, Tianming Sha, Qizheng Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench evaluates LLM agents' capabilities in autonomously engineering RL post-training pipelines, revealing both intelligent behaviors and significant limitations across various tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: We introduce Agent^2 RL-Bench, a compact diagnostic benchmark for evaluating agentic RL post-training, which tests whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and execute post-training pipelines that improve foundation models. RL post-training increasingly drives model alignment and specialization, yet existing benchmarks are largely static, rewarding supervised fine-tuning or script generation without assessing an agent's ability to close an interactive RL loop. Agent^2 RL-Bench provides a unified agent-facing interface: each run starts from an isolated workspace containing a base model, task data, instructions, and a grading API, and agents must iterate within a fixed budget by training models and submitting artifacts for evaluation. The benchmark spans six tasks across three levels, from static rule-based training to judge-based optimization and closed-loop online RL with trajectory collection. Two diagnostic skills, namely runtime recording and post-hoc summarization, enable structured analysis of agent behavior, facilitating smooth and effective iteration of the benchmark's evaluation framework. Across five agent systems and six driver LLMs, agents show intelligent behavior but clear limitations: one RL-oriented run improves ALFWorld from 4.85 to 93.28 via SFT warm-up and GRPO with online rollouts, yet DeepSearchQA remains difficult, most successful routes rely on supervised pipelines, and interactive outcomes show large differences across agent stacks. Overall, Agent2 RL-Bench shows that current agents can sometimes engineer online RL, but stable agent-driven RL post-training remains rare under fixed budgets. It also demonstrates that our benchmark provides a strong and effective evaluation framework for future research in this direction. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Bo Li, Taoyong Cui, Bob Zhang, Mengran Li, Chengyang Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: WeightCode introduces Weight-Space Programming to enhance neural networks' capabilities by directly modifying weights with executable programs, achieving significant performance improvements without retraining.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original command and navigation capabilities. On ImageNet, four weight programs achieve net gains of 8.84-17.62 points while preserving clean accuracy, outperforming the best of eight fine-tuning methods under matched examples, checks, and retention constraints. In a Vision Transformer, causal interventions show that installed noise-correction gates drive robustness gains, while their selective activation preserves clean accuracy. Rerun on five independently trained Vision Transformers without further language model calls, ten weight programs retain 83-110% of their source-network gains on average, whereas copying their fixed weight edits yields negligible gains. Six programs written for an already edited network add 5.23-14.50 points of contrast robustness while retaining the previously installed noise gain. Together, these results establish WSP as a new route to acquiring and accumulating capabilities in trained neural networks through reusable weight programs.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent framework that optimizes memory retention through local verification, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoran Ye, Yuxing Lu, Haonan Dong, Zhaochen Su, Guojie Song
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: Harness-Zero enables agent harness distillation by using an optimized harness to guide training, enhancing model performance and behavior recovery while eliminating the need for specialized harnesses at deployment.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: (1) For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness. (2) With the specialized harness removed at deployment, Harness-Zero improves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached, while reducing inference token usage by 27%-86%. (3) Harness-Zero recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Boyu Chen, Jiaqi Liang, Xini Ding
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: GroundingPI is a state-of-the-art grounding foundation model that enhances physical intelligence in robotics by improving object localization and manipulation through advanced multimodal training techniques.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: GroundAnything: Reconciling Parallel Decoding with Precise Visual Grounding at Flash Speed
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Qize Yu, Lianrui Fan, Bowen Ping, Xini Ding, Zetian Song
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: GroundAnything is a 4B-parameter model that achieves fast, precise visual grounding through parallel decoding and iterative denoising, outperforming existing models on multiple benchmarks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Autoregressive (AR) grounding models serialize spatial predictions, introducing sequential latency and imposing a causal order on output tokens. We view grounding as visual evidence extraction: objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query, yet their dependencies do not imply an intrinsic left-to-right generation order. This distinction makes bidirectional diffusion a natural fit, allowing spatial hypotheses to emerge in parallel and be jointly refined through iterative denoising. We introduce GroundAnything, a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model that reconciles fast parallel decoding with precise localization through blockwise denoising. Training combines grounding pretraining from public datasets and dedicated data engines, direct AR-to-diffusion conversion with joint AR and diffusion objectives, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO-based reinforcement post-training. Across 30 grounding benchmarks, our autoregressive variant, GroundAnything-VLM, establishes a new overall state of the art among similarly sized models at 72.42%, remaining competitive with GPT-6 Astra (71.35%). With entropy-guided decoding, GroundAnything also surpasses the prior state of the art at this scale, averaging 61.75% versus 53.32% for the fast MTP-based LocateAnything model. We further explore decoding strategies, showing that an optional self-speculative mode achieves a 4.51$\times$ speedup over the AR counterpart with a 0.74 percentage-point drop in COCO F1mIoU. Infrastructure experiments show that progressive inference optimizations translate parallel decoding into practical speedups. These gains support efficient visual grounding in latency-sensitive real-world systems.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: TacInno introduces a novel approach to enhance Vision-Language-Action models by using tactile innovation as a training target, significantly improving manipulation success rates.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Xu, Yifu Yuan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SpatialScout-V2 enhances active mapping in real 3D environments, revealing significant challenges in object localization accuracy among various vision-language models.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires agents to acquire visual evidence and integrate partial observations into coherent three-dimensional representations. We introduce SpatialScout-V2, which extends SpatialScout's active mapping task from simulation to real residential scenes through three advances: real visual observations, preservation of original scene content, and interactive exploration of recorded views. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, the benchmark covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories. Given a fixed target inventory, agents autonomously select recorded viewpoints and viewing directions, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively estimate and revise object centers within a fixed interaction budget. We evaluate the localization accuracy and completeness of object-center maps using mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models (VLMs), we find that six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20\%. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches only 22.52\%, with just 18.36\% of targets exceeding an IoU of 0.5. Further analysis shows that broad submission coverage can coexist with limited localization accuracy, while target omissions further reduce overall scores. These results highlight substantial challenges in constructing accurate and complete object-center maps through active exploration of real scenes.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Bingqing Jiang, Guoxi Zhang, Jasper Wang, Bingning Wang, Difan Zou
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO) to enhance multimodal reasoning in vision-language models by assigning role-specific credit to perception and reasoning tokens.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), especially with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has shown strong potential for improving the reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs). However, in multimodal reasoning, final-answer rewards are typically assigned at the sequence level and do not distinguish the functional roles of different tokens, making it difficult to determine whether a correct answer is supported by task-relevant visual evidence. In this paper, we revisit multimodal RLVR from the perspective of role-aware token-level credit assignment, where structured responses are decomposed into perception tokens for extracting visual evidence and reasoning tokens for deriving answers from that evidence. Based on this perspective, we propose Structured Role-aware Policy Optimization (SRPO), which refines the sequence-level GRPO advantage into role-aware token-level advantages without changing the reward function. Specifically, SRPO assigns role-specific credit by using self-distilled on-policy contrasts: perception tokens are emphasized according to their visual dependency under original versus corrupted visual inputs, while reasoning tokens are emphasized according to their consistency with the generated perception. These role-specific signals are further unified through a shared trajectory-level baseline, yielding positive token weights that adjust relative update magnitudes while preserving the original GRPO reward and advantage signs, without requiring external reward models or separate teachers. Experiments across diverse multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that SRPO improves evidence-grounded reasoning, highlighting the importance of moving beyond uniform sequence-level credit toward role-aware optimization for reliable multimodal reasoning.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RoboForge: Cross-space Motion Refinement for Physically Executable Humanoid Whole-body Tracking
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Xichen Yuan, Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Xinying Guo
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RoboForge enhances humanoid robot motion tracking by refining motion references through a data-centric framework, improving tracking success rates and enabling complex dynamic movements.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Whole-body motion tracking has rapidly expanded the skill repertoire of humanoid robots, yet nearly all of this progress has come from stronger tracking policies, while the motion references they imitate are treated as fixed supervision. We argue that reference quality is a first-order factor in tracking performance. Human motion data carry capture and estimation artifacts, and retargeting adds physical inconsistencies due to the human-robot embodiment gap; discarding such motions sacrifices valuable skill content, whereas retaining them uncorrected undermines policy learning. We present RoboForge, a data-centric framework that resolves this dilemma by refining references instead of filtering them, repairing each error in the space where it arises. In human motion space, a quality-guided diffusion model localizes corrupted segments and inpaints only those segments, leaving the rest of the motion intact. In robot motion space, kinematic repair corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects, and annealed sampling-based optimization under physics rollouts turns kinematically plausible references into dynamically executable ones. RoboForge requires no change to the tracker: it improves three retargeting methods and four tracking policies, raising the success rate of BeyondMimic from 89.51% to 96.20% while reducing the mean per-joint position error (MPJPE-L) by 31.6%. Refined references also accelerate policy learning, restore tracking performance from heavily corrupted inputs, and enable more than 30 high-dynamic motions, including flips and the Thomas flare, on a real Unitree G1.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Chenhao Wu, Zixiang Ni
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper diagnoses failures in visual world-model planners as either search or scoring issues, proposing tailored remedies to improve planning outcomes across various environments.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.
